A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronic and electrocatalytic properties of MOFs can be rationally designed by tuning the metal atoms.
the bifunctional oxygen evolution/reduction electrocatalysts can be rationally designed based on MOFs by controlling the central metal atom and the metal ratio.
the bifunctional oxygen catalysts can be rationally designed through bimetal centers in MOF materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electronic and electrocatalytic properties of MOF-based bifunctional oxygen catalysts can be tuned by the central metal atoms, and the bifunctional catalysis of MOF materials can be achieved by combining different central metal atoms.
bifunctional oxygen catalysts can be designed by combining different active sites in the same material, which can be used as a guide for the experimental design of new bifunctional oxygen electrodes.

the electronic and electrocatalytic properties of MOF nanosheets are highly dependent on the central metal atom, which provides guidance for the rational design of efficient bifuctional oxygen electrocataysts.
